extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: Delaware's Landlord-Tenant Code (Title 25) prohibits self-help lockouts, but its detailed provisions and penalties are written for residential rental units. No confirmed commercial-specific wrongful-lockout penalty statute or multiplier was found; treat as actual damages only pending confirmation.

outcome.description: The Magistrate's final post-trial report recommended judgment for the estate and against the occupant for $44,000.00 on the estate's unjust-enrichment counterclaim ($1,000 per month for the Dock Street Properties from May 2020 through August 2022, plus $1,000 per month agreed rent for the Commerce Property from April 2021 through August 2022), rejecting the $5,000-per-month / $160,000 demand, denying the occupant's own $70,000 unjust-enrichment claim, and denying the estate's trespass counterclaim; costs to the estate as prevailing party, no attorney's fees.
outcome.appellateChange: none - trial-level magistrate's final report (exceptions available under Court of Chancery Rule 144); no appellate ruling in this document

source.court: Delaware Court of Chancery (Magistrate in Chancery, final post-trial report)
source.excerptNote: Verbatim sentences from Part I (Background, subsections A-F: early years, use and occupancy, attempted purchase, Commerce Property, falling out, procedural history) plus the paragraph of Part II.A that lays out each side's unjust-enrichment demand and the occupant's two responsive arguments. Removed: the introduction and conclusion stating the recommended judgment; every 'I find' / 'I recommend' sentence; the magistrate's rental-value estimate and month-by-month computation; the trespass ruling; footnote citations and record cites. PDF line-break and word-split artifacts were normalized; no wording changed.
